claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO introduces strong phonon-scattering centers by disrupting lattice periodicity.
SRO-induced scattering dominates over a potential reduction in phonon group velocity caused by local stiffening.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed initial MoNbTaW-like alloy is chemically random and has no significant chemical clustering.
MoNbTaW can display a significant energetic driving force for chemical SRO.
Controlled annealing or quenching can induce SRO in MoNbTaW-like RHEAs without causing long-range phase separation.
The targeted SRO can consist of Mo-Nb or Ta-W pairs.
SRO remains stable throughout 300–1200 K in the proposed alloy.
Dislocation mobility is active over the proposed 300–1200 K interval.
Nanoscale SRO domains create atomic-scale mass-fluctuation and force-constant disorder that acts as resonant scattering centers for mid-to-high-frequency phonons.
Transitioning from a random solid solution to an SRO state increases the variance of local atomic environments.
SRO-induced local bond stiffening may increase phonon group velocity.
SRO-induced mass and force-constant variations reduce phonon mean free path more than local stiffening increases group velocity.
The SRO sample will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than the chemically disordered sample.
The conductivity suppression will be strongest at 300–800 K because phonon-phonon scattering is less dominant there than defect or cluster scattering.
Above 1000 K, Umklapp scattering may dominate and mask the influence of SRO.
The proposed regime requires coherent SRO clusters smaller than 5 nm and excludes macroscopic phase separation or long-range ordered precipitates.
Annealing MoNbTaW at 800 K for 100 hours will maximize SRO.

An equal or higher thermal conductivity in the confirmed-SRO sample below 1000 K, relative to a composition- and grain-size-matched disordered control, is designated as falsifying the predicted suppression.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis refers to a reduction in phonon group velocity caused by local stiffening, whereas the mechanism says local stiffening may increase phonon group velocity.

Rapid quenching from a high-temperature state is described both as a route to retain SRO and as a route to freeze a chemically disordered state; the distinct thermodynamic or kinetic conditions needed to obtain these opposite states are not specified.
